proof_of_candidate_semantics: Background: both constructors leave >= 1 full row and >= 1 full column of background between quadrants (native rowthick, colthick >= 2; RE-ARC di, dj >= 2). Any full row crosses the vertical band and any full column crosses the horizontal band, so no quadrant colour has both. The background is the unique colour with both.
Odd colour box is pure: its cells lie in one corner quadrant, which holds only it and background (native quad assignment; RE-ARC fill(trg)).

RE-ARC shared colour is impure: subf puts a cell on all four edges of each of its three quadrant boxes, and any three corner quadrants touch all four grid edges. Its box is the whole grid and contains the odd colour's cells.
Native shared colour: impure unless its 0.9-density quadrants are almost empty. Then both boxes are pure and the program raises. It never returns a wrong grid.

Label equality: native output crops the rarest non-zero colour's box. Its selection loop forces that colour to be the odd colour. RE-ARC output is subgrid(trg), and subf makes the odd colour's box equal trg.

minimal_native_counterexample.construction: generate(width=15, height=15, colors=<grid>); row=col=5, rowthick=colthick=2, odd quadrant 3 (bottom-right) fully painted
